reads.monthly_note:
May was the month the income floor showed. Two Guida paychecks at the lower ~$1,590 rate (vs March's $2,980 catch-up check) brought income to $7,382 — the dataset low. Meanwhile, spending held at $8,958 on recurring commitments plus a Taylor Dance payment ($220) and elevated utility costs (two DTE payments in one cycle).

Liquid balance dropped from $5,230 to $3,653, giving back most of April's surplus. The $500 investment transfer continued to Schwab. Debt service stayed at the baseline $298.

The pattern emerging across March–May: income swings significantly month to month depending on paycheck count and Guida pay amounts, while spending stays in a tighter band around $8,000–9,000. Months with only four paychecks and the lower Guida rate run deficits; months with an extra paycheck run surpluses. The household's fiscal balance is more sensitive to paycheck timing than to spending discipline.
